original_statement:
Let $F(t,x,\lambda)$ be smooth in $(x,\lambda)$ on an open time-state-parameter
domain. Near any base data $(t_0,x_0,\lambda_0)$ there are a compact time
interval $I$ and a neighbourhood $W$ of $(x_0,\lambda_0)$ such that, for every
$(y,\lambda)\in W$, the solution of

$$x'(t)=F(t,x(t),\lambda),\qquad x(t_0)=y,$$

is defined on $I$, and the resulting solution map is smooth in the pair
$(y,\lambda)$.

counterexample.regularity: For each fixed t this is constant, hence C∞, in(x,lambda), exactly the stated weak premise.
counterexample.proof: A classical local solution has a nondegenerate interval around0. On each side of0 its derivative is0, so MVT makes it constant there. Differentiability at0 implies continuity, so both constants equal x(0), making it constant throughout a neighbourhood. Its derivative at0 is therefore0, contradicting the equation requiring1. This does not rely on failure of derivative continuity; no differentiable solution exists.

Its operative variational proof is valid here: all state derivatives of G are jointly continuous, compact cylinders bound them, and the C1 difference-quotient/Gronwall estimate is uniform in time. The C1 initial-data theorem applied to these jointly smooth jet systems gives C1 dependence of the entire jet (including the highest component); uniqueness identifies those components with actual derivatives obtained from the Volterra equation.
